newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH KEEPS AUSTRALIA ON PATH TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH KEEPS AUSTRALIA ON PATH TO VICTORY.

text.p: Another gritty innings by Steve Waugh, looking set for his second century of the match, carried Australia closer on Saturday to a third test win that would level the Ashes series.

By the end of the third day at Old Trafford, Australia were 262 for six, an overall lead of 335. England had earlier lost their last two wickets for the addition of only one run to be all out for 162 in their first innings.
Leg-spinner Shane Warne accounted for one of them to finish with figures of six for 48.
Initially aided by twin brother Mark (55) in a fourth-wicket partnership of 92, Steve Waugh, although troubled by a hand injury, followed his first innings 108 with an unbeaten 82.
Seamer Dean Headley, who took four wickets in the first innings, was again England's most successful bowler with three of the Australian wickets to fall.

Among them were both openers, captain Mark Taylor (one) and Matthew Elliott (11). Greg Blewett was the third man to fall with the total on 39, given out to a debatable catch by Nasser Hussain in the slips off spinner Robert Croft.
But the Waugh's then rebuilt the Australian innings and Ian Healy (47) and Warne (33 not out) maintained the momentum.
